title: The board and the starting position
summary: Orient the board correctly and set up all 32 pieces.

steps.md:
Chess is played on an 8x8 board of 64 squares, alternating light and dark. Two rules fix the setup:

1. **Light on the right**: the corner square nearest each player's right hand is light.
2. **Queen on her own colour**: the white queen starts on a light square, the black queen on a dark one.

The goal of the game is checkmate: attacking the enemy king so that it has no escape. You will learn exactly what that means in a later lesson.

The starting position. From the corners inwards on the back rank: rook, knight, bishop, then queen and king in the middle. Eight pawns stand in front. Black mirrors White: queens face each other, kings face each other.

steps.question: You sit down at the board as White. Which corner square must be on your right-hand side?
steps.explain: "Light on the right". If the near-right corner is dark, the board is turned the wrong way and the kings and queens will end up on the wrong squares.

steps.question: Where does the white queen start?
choices: On the light square next to the king (d1)
On the dark square next to the king (e1)
steps.explain: Queen on her own colour: the white queen goes on the light central square of the back rank, d1. The king takes the square beside her, e1.

steps.question: And the black queen?
choices: Directly opposite the white queen, on a dark square (d8)
steps.explain: The black queen also stands on her own colour, the dark square d8, facing the white queen across the board.

steps.question: What is wrong with this setup?
choices: Kings and queens have swapped squares
The knights and bishops have swapped squares
The pawns are on the wrong rank
steps.explain: Here each queen is on the opposite colour (white queen on a dark square). This mistake shows up often. Check that each queen is on her own colour.

steps.question: Which piece stands right next to each rook at the start?
steps.explain: From the corner: rook, knight, bishop. A common setup error is swapping knights and bishops.

steps.prompt: White always moves first. Make a first move: push the pawn in front of your king forward two squares.
steps.hint: The king stands on the e-file; its pawn is directly in front of it.
steps.explain: Every pawn may move two squares on its very first move. You have just played 1.e4, the most popular first move in chess.

steps.question: Retrieval check: how many pawns does each side start with?
steps.explain: Each side has 16 units: 8 pawns plus king, queen, two rooks, two bishops and two knights.

steps.question: Retrieval check: what are the two setup rules?
choices: Light square on the right; queen on her own colour
Dark square on the right; king on his own colour
Rooks in the middle; queen on the left
steps.explain: Light on the right, queen on her own colour. If you get those two right, everything else falls into place.
